recipes.name: Gizzada
steps: Rub butter into flour and add cold water to form a pastry dough; chill 20 minutes.
Simmer coconut, sugar, ginger and nutmeg with 60 ml water until thickened, then cool.
Roll pastry into circles, pinch rims into small cups and fill with cooled coconut mixture.
Bake at 180°C/355°F for 20–25 minutes until pastry is cooked.

recipes.name: Grater cake
steps: Line a heatproof tray with parchment.
Simmer coconut, sugar and water in a heavy pan, stirring often.
Cook until liquid largely evaporates and mass forms a thick sticky paste; stir in vanilla.
Press into a shallow tray, optionally tint half, and cut after cooling.

recipes.name: Peanut drops
steps: Line a baking tray with parchment.
Boil sugar and water until syrup thickens.
Stir in roasted peanuts and ginger and continue cooking until syrup coats nuts thickly.
Drop spoonfuls onto tray and cool fully; boiling sugar causes severe burns.

recipes.name: Plantain tart
steps: Rub butter into flour, moisten with cold water, and refrigerate dough for 20 minutes.
Mash cooked, softened ripe plantains with sugar, cinnamon and lime; cool filling.
Roll dough and cut eight rounds, add filling and fold edges closed.
Bake at 190°C/375°F until pastry is golden and thoroughly cooked, about 25 minutes.

recipes.name: Sweet potato pone
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C/350°F and grease a baking dish.
Mix grated sweet potato with coconut milk, sugar, flour and spices.
Spoon into dish and level surface.
Bake approximately 65–85 minutes until set throughout; cool before cutting.

recipes.name: Cassava pone
ingredients: 700 g commercially processed food-safe grated cassava
steps: Use only food-safe processed grated cassava and follow product instructions.
Mix cassava, coconut milk, sugar, flour and flavorings.
Pour into greased baking dish and spread evenly.
Bake at 175°C/350°F for 65–85 minutes until cooked and set; cool thoroughly.

recipes.name: Asham
steps: Toast cornmeal slowly in a dry heavy skillet, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly colored.
Cool completely, then grind further if coarse.
Mix with sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Serve dry in small portions or sprinkle over fruit; avoid inhaling fine powder.

recipes.name: Blue draws (duckunoo)
steps: Clean banana leaves carefully and briefly soften over steam or low heat until flexible.
Mix cornmeal, coconut, sweet potato, sugar and spices into a moist paste, adding water by spoonful if needed.
Place small portions on leaf squares and wrap securely with food-safe ties.
Steam over simmering water for approximately 60–80 minutes until centers are fully cooked; cool before opening.

recipes.name: Toto cake
steps: Heat oven to 175°C/350°F; line a cake pan.
Combine flour, baking powder, nutmeg and sugar.
Fold in grated coconut, coconut milk and vanilla to form thick batter.
Bake 35–45 minutes until a skewer comes out without wet batter.

recipes.name: Black cake
ingredients: 200 ml dark rum or fruit juice
steps: Soak dried fruit in rum or juice, refrigerate as appropriate, then finely chop or puree.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, then fold in flour, baking powder and cinnamon.
Fold in fruit and browning, pour into prepared deep cake tin.
Bake at 150°C/300°F for 90–120 minutes until center is set; cool completely before slicing.

recipes.name: Rum cake
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C/350°F and grease a bundt or loaf tin.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, baking powder, milk, vanilla and rum.
Bake about 40–55 minutes until skewer comes out clean; cool and label alcohol content.

recipes.name: Guava cheese
steps: Cook peeled guava with a little water until soft, then strain to remove all hard seeds.
Measure 500 g pulp, add sugar and lime, and simmer in a heavy pot.
Stir constantly as mixture thickens and begins to pull from sides.
Pour into buttered heatproof dish, cool completely and slice; boiling fruit sugar is hazardous.

recipes.name: Irish moss drink
ingredients: 40 g commercially cleaned dried edible sea moss
steps: Rinse commercially prepared food-grade sea moss well according to package guidance.
Simmer in water until softened and thickening, about 20–30 minutes, then cool slightly.
Blend with milk, vanilla, nutmeg and sugar until smooth, using heat-safe methods.
Refrigerate promptly and serve chilled; check iodine and ingredient restrictions for consumers.

recipes.name: Carrot juice Jamaican style
steps: Wash, peel and chop carrots.
Cook carrots in water until tender, then cool.
Blend with some cooking liquid until smooth and strain if desired.
Stir in milk, ginger, nutmeg and sugar; chill promptly.

recipes.name: Peanut punch
steps: Blend roasted peanuts with 400 ml water until very smooth.
Strain if a fine texture is desired.
Add remaining water, milk, nutmeg, vanilla and sugar and blend again.
Chill immediately and label prominently as containing peanuts.

recipes.name: June plum juice
steps: Wash fruit thoroughly, cut flesh away from large fibrous stones.
Blend flesh with water until pulpy.
Strain through a sieve and discard fibrous material.
Stir in sugar and lime to taste, chill and serve.

recipes.name: Tamarind juice
steps: Check tamarind for shell and seed fragments.
Soak pulp in warm water and break up with a spoon.
Strain to remove fibers and remaining solids.
Sweeten, add ginger if preferred, chill and serve.

recipes.name: Coconut water
ingredients: 2 to 3 fresh drinking coconuts with approximately 1 L clear water total
steps: Wash outside of coconuts carefully before cutting.
Open using a clean, appropriate tool on a stable surface; avoid injury from sharp machetes.
Pour clear water into clean cups and check for off odors.
Consume promptly or refrigerate immediately; discard spoiled or discolored liquid.

recipes.name: Mauby
ingredients: 30 g commercially sold edible mauby bark
steps: Rinse mauby bark according to supplier instructions.
Simmer bark, cinnamon and allspice in water for 15–20 minutes.
Cool covered, strain and sweeten to balance bitterness.
Refrigerate and serve cold; use food-grade bark from a reputable supplier.

recipes.name: Cerasee tea
steps: Use only a correctly identified, commercially food-grade product.
Bring water to boil, remove from heat and add dried leaves.
Steep covered briefly according to supplier instructions and strain.
Serve in small amounts; pregnancy, medications and blood sugar conditions warrant clinical advice rather than treating this as a medicine.

recipes.name: Guava jam
steps: Wash, chop and simmer guavas in water until very soft.
Press pulp through sieve to remove seeds.
Cook pulp with sugar and lime until thick enough to coat spoon.
Transfer to clean containers, cool and refrigerate; this is refrigerator jam, not validated shelf-stable canning.

recipes.name: June plum chutney
steps: Chop fruit and onion finely.
Combine vinegar, sugar, fruit, onion and seasonings in a saucepan.
Simmer gently 35–50 minutes, stirring until mixture thickens.
Cool and refrigerate in clean containers; not a shelf-stable canning procedure.

recipes.name: Pepper sauce
steps: Wear gloves and avoid touching face while handling hot peppers.
Chop peppers, onion and garlic; simmer with vinegar until softened.
Cool slightly, then blend carefully using a heat-safe method.
Refrigerate in a clean container; this is a refrigerated condiment, not a validated shelf-stable preservation recipe.
